Some summer updates: 1. I got to attend Y Combinator Startup School in San Francisco, and hear from various technology leaders on a variety of topics. One idea I found quite interesting was in Dmitri Dolgov's (Waymo Co-CEO) talk on physical AI, where he spoke about scaling demos to products as a game of 9s. The point was that every additional 9 in performance/efficiency/reliability required doing something fundamentally differently (99 --> 99.9, etc), and I thought this was especially relevant today in the context of AI coding tools. AI coding tools can quickly get to an initial set of 9s but building scalable physical AI products requires more effort, and I thought this rule of 9s described that balance quite well. 2. I got my own SO-101 robotic arm, and have been training it to do various tasks. I've been documenting my progress here: https://lnkd.in/gfsj8DpT 3. I finished my summer internship at Humana , working within the Primary Care Organization team and developing an AI service which pulls patient data and evaluates prescription renewal requests. It was quite cool to actually see our service populate notes on the real electronic health record system, and cite the information used in the final determination. I wanted to thank Mohammed Inayathullah , my manager, for guiding me through this project and giving me a great summer experience!

The hack reported by OpenAI and Hugging Face is a direct result of the lack of data quality practices coming from RL environments. RLVR is an extremely powerful tool that has brought us into superhuman coding agents and more. But that’s the problem: They are extremely powerful optimizers, and will do anything to receive a reward. Every benchmark, every RL environment, and every verifier is a potential attack surface. Even SWE-bench Verified had a bug in it for over one and a half years where part of the GitHub history was leaking. What have we done about this? 1. We published a paper back in April about verifying the verifiers. We were the first to do so. 2. We released SWE-Marathon, which is focusing on reward hacking in the ultra-long horizon setting. 3. We published blog posts about reward hacking and are working with numerous partners to increase visibility of this issue. There’s a lot more work to be done here. If you want to work on high-impact problems like this, check our careers page - my DMs are open.

I used to think I was ambitious, then I came to San Francisco. I met people who genuinely believed they were going to change how an entire industry works, and meant it. These were people betting years of their lives on ideas that, by any reasonable measure, probably wouldn't work. And they talked about it like it was already done. It was contagious. You sit across from someone who casually assumes they'll win, and your own sense of what's possible changes. I didn't get more talented by being around them. My baseline for what's "normal" moved. This is the most underrated reason to put yourself in rooms you don't fully belong in yet. Spend enough time around people who refuse to be realistic and you slowly stop being so realistic yourself :) Photo: Golden Gate Bridge with Friends

Excited to share that I’ve wrapped up my first two weeks as a Go-to-Market Intern at Daytona !! It’s been an incredible start, and I’m especially grateful to Borna Perak for making the recruiting and onboarding process so smooth. This summer, I’ll be working on reinforcement learning solutions powered by Daytona’s infrastructure, exploring how scalable cloud environments can support RL training and evaluation for computer-use agents. I’m excited to dive deeper into the intersection of AI infrastructure and RL and share what I learn along the way. --- This past weekend was also a highlight: I had the opportunity to represent Daytona as a sponsor at the YC × HUD Hackathon. It was amazing meeting so many talented builders and seeing the projects everyone put together. If you’re around San Francisco this week, come say hi at AI Engineer World’s Fair 2026! And if you’d like to follow along with what I’m building this summer, I’ll be sharing updates on X: https://x.com/hanabenko . Looking forward to an exciting summer!!!! <3
